page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 32 vCPUs and 32 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the server bundles three NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs, delivering a total of 144 GB of VRAM. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. The CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 4190.38 and a multi-core score of 132459.57, both placing in the top tier. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 3003.0 and a multi-core score of 27001.0. Memory performance is strong, with a read-only large block bandwidth of 331.99 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 123.17 GB/sec. The server demonstrates high capability in LLM inference, processing 13662.51 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 6061.83 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. Redis SET operations reached 128.07 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput was measured at 97.51 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the lack of local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data. Additionally, the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce performance variability under sustained CPU-bound workloads. However, the high density of GPU resources and memory makes it a highly cost-efficient option for workloads requiring massive parallel processing without the overhead of dedicated physical CPU cores. This server is suited for LLM inference, machine learning workloads, image processing, ray tracing, and database operations.
